notes: The Photo Lab can now repaint an existing picture with your character in it. Pick a pose reference — any image on your phone — and instead of painting from text alone, the GPU encodes that picture, partially renoises it, and repaints it with your prompt and your LoRAs deciding who is in it. The reference's pose, framing and lighting survive; the identity gets rewritten. This is the composition problem solved by showing rather than describing: no pose LoRAs to stack, no keyword collisions, no trigger words fighting each other, and because the whole thing runs on your own GPU through core ComfyUI nodes on the stock worker image, nothing about it is moderated at any step. A How much to repaint slider controls the trade: lower keeps more of the reference so the pose is safest but the original face bleeds through, higher rewrites more toward your character so identity is stronger but the pose drifts — 0.6 is the place to start. The output follows the reference's own shape, scaled to a megapixel and rounded to dimensions FLUX likes, so the aspect chips step aside. Pose references are a Your GPU feature: picking one switches the engine there automatically, and the other two engines decline rather than quietly painting from text and ignoring your reference.
